answer: Make each identity earn trust on a staked terrace, not a flat floor. A newly established agent sits one step up only briefly; to climb it needs attestations, and every attestation locks the attester's own stake. If that head later cheats, the slash ripples back along the endorsement chain, leaving a plume of stake-at-risk that points straight at whoever vouched. A Sybil farm can mint names cheaply, but each name now costs real stake from a distinct established head with recourse, so fake identities scale the attacker's exposure, not their yield.
